subject.title: [Architecture] Migration of transient plugin state to Agent-Scoped SQLite cache tables

question: Should external plugins receive a public agent-scoped persistent cache API, and if so should it extend existing plugin KV or become a separate cache surface?
rationale: Storage mechanics cannot determine the permanent SDK boundary, tenant-isolation model, quotas, value and TTL semantics, or whether restart loss is intentionally acceptable for some transient state.

options.title: Extend plugin KV carefully
options.body: Add agent-scoped namespaces to the existing plugin-state contract with explicit identity, isolation, quotas, serialization, TTL cleanup, and upgrade tests.

options.title: Keep current surfaces
options.body: Use existing plugin KV for durable state and reserve in-memory structures for rebuildable process-local caches, supported by clearer documentation and examples.

options.title: Design a separate cache API
options.body: Create a distinct cache contract only after concrete plugin inventory proves existing KV semantics insufficient and maintainers approve its compatibility obligations.

recommendation.title: Extend plugin KV carefully
recommendation.body: Add agent-scoped namespaces to the existing plugin-state contract with explicit identity, isolation, quotas, serialization, TTL cleanup, and upgrade tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history assessment most directly connects steipete to recent plugin-state storage work and the relevant public SDK boundary.
